entries.proposition: WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS, AND ITS SIZE. It is the EDITOR'S INTRODUCTION to a nine-chapter multi-author review of common fragile sites in Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences 71(23), pages 4487-4488 — TWO PAGES, single-authored by R I Aqeilan, who is also the author of chapter 8. Body of 7,211 characters. It contains no experiment, no figure, no table and no supplement; its content is a map of nine other papers plus a short history of the field.
entries.snippet: The present multi-author-review comprises nine contributions that cover all-important aspects of understanding CFS and some of their corresponding genes.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE GENRE IS FIXED BY A DATE PAIR, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS ACROSS THIS WAVE. Received and accepted on the SAME DAY. That is the signature of an invited editorial introduction, not of an externally refereed review — and it is checkable rather than inferred. It matters because the metadata says otherwise: PubMed assigns publication types 'review-article, Review, Journal Article' and the PMC deposit carries article-type="review-article". PubMed's Review tag OVER-describes a two-page editor's introduction. On this actor's other wave-5 paper, PMID 27551470, PubMed's bare 'Journal Article' UNDER-described an editorial that PMC deposits as one. TWO PAPERS, ONE WAVE, PUBLICATION-TYPE METADATA WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS — which is a standing caution for any triage that routes on pubtype.

🔴 PRINCIPAL FINDING OF THIS READING, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FIELD RATHER THAN ABOUT THIS PAPER. The document opens by dividing fragile sites in two and assigning HUMAN GENETIC DISORDERS to the RARE class and CANCER to the COMMON class. WWOX spans FRA16D, a COMMON fragile site; the genotype class this repository models is a Mendelian, recessively inherited human genetic disorder of WWOX. Under the taxonomy the field organises itself by, the WWOX germline disorder falls on the WRONG SIDE of the dichotomy that defines this entire literature. This is not a criticism of the sentence, which is a correct statement about fragile-site classification. It is the STRUCTURAL EXPLANATION for a measured absence — see the neuro screen recorded beside it — and it tells this repository something it can act on: the CFS literature is where WWOX's molecular biology lives, and it is organised in a way that guarantees the WWOX phenotype will not appear there.
entries.snippet: Rare fragile sites are seen in a small proportion of individuals, inherited in a Mendelian manner and are associated with human genetic disorders. In contrast, common fragile sites (CFS) are present in all individuals, represent the largest class of fragile sites and are largely involved in cancer.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THE PRECEDING FINDING MORE THAN A READING OF ONE SENTENCE. Screened over the 7,211-character body with the reference list separated off first: epilep 0, seizure 0, brain 0, CNS 0, WOREE 0, encephalopath 0, ataxia 0, intellectual 0, recessive 0, syndrome 0, germline 0, and 'neuro' 0 — LITERALLY ZERO ON ALL TWELVE. The two near-misses are 'patient', which occurs once and refers to Dekaban's 1965 irradiated woman, and 'inherit', which occurs once in the sentence quoted here about RARE fragile sites. This is the introduction to a nine-chapter review whose chapter 8 is entirely about WWOX, published in December 2014, by which time WWOX germline disease was described in the literature. The absence is total and it is structural, not accidental. It reproduces, on a second document and a different author, exactly the result this repository measured on PMID 24510053 (zero across the same term set over 38,845 characters).
entries.snippet: This “weak” region is known today as fragile site.
entries.anchor: Body, paragraph 1 — the sentence that closes the historical framing, quoted as the anchor for a screen over the whole body

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE EDITOR NAMES THE GAP THAT IS EXACTLY THIS REPOSITORY'S LAYER. In 2014, the person best placed to know states that the GENE PRODUCTS of common fragile sites — as opposed to the fragility mechanisms — are under-studied. Eight of the nine chapters he then introduces are about mechanism, replication, timing or mapping; two are about a gene product (FHIT, WWOX). The sentence is worth keeping because it is a dated, first-hand statement of where the field's attention was NOT.
entries.snippet: Of note, little light is shed on the gene products of CFS and their role in tumor suppression and genomic instability.

entries.proposition: 🔴 CROSS-DOCUMENT FINDING, AND IT ONLY EXISTS BECAUSE BOTH WAVE-5 PAPERS WERE READ. Here, in 2014, the editor reports chapter 6 as having CONCLUDED that CFS fragility is 'unlikely only a structural passive incident'. Thirteen months later the same senior author publishes PMID 27551470, which frames passive-versus-active as a live two-sided controversy — and cites this very chapter (Georgakilas, PMID 25238782) as its ref 6, for the 'sensors' proposal it builds on. STATED CAREFULLY, BECAUSE THE OVERCLAIM IS AVAILABLE AND WRONG: one special issue leaning one way does not settle a field controversy, and an author is entitled to present a question as open. What is recorded is the narrower fact — the framing shifted from 'concluded' to 'debatable' inside one author's own output across thirteen months, and the 2015 piece's own citation for the point is the chapter described here as having concluded it.
entries.snippet: It is finally concluded that fragility of CFS is unlikely only a structural “passive” incident but an event which might have a profound biological effect.

entries.proposition: THE EDITOR SUMMARISES HIS OWN GROUP'S CHAPTER AMONG THE NINE. Chapter 8 is PMID 25245215, authored by Aqeilan, Abu-Remaileh and Abu-Odeh — and the introduction that summarises it is single-authored by Aqeilan. This is ordinary practice for a guest-edited issue and is recorded for WEIGHTING, not as an impropriety: the summary of chapter 8 is an author's account of his own work and carries no independent editorial judgement, whereas the other eight summaries do. 🔴 OPERATIONALLY RELEVANT TO THIS REPOSITORY: PMID 25245215 is in this actor's own lot on AQEILAN-FT-B-001, unread and unclaimed, and this reading establishes that it is the single most valuable unread item in that lot — it is the field's dedicated WWOX chapter.
entries.snippet: In chapter 8, contributed by the Aqeilan group, the emerging roles of WWOX, product of FRA16D, in tumor suppression and genome stability are discussed.

entries.proposition: WHAT CHAPTER 8 IS REPORTED TO CONCLUDE — RECORDED AS A POINTER, NOT AS EVIDENCE. This is a one-sentence restatement of an unread paper by that paper's own author. It is not a finding about WWOX and must not be entered as one; it is the specification of what PMID 25245215 will have to be checked against when it is read. Note the scope of the conclusion as stated: 'functionally required for cell homeostasis' and consequences for 'the neoplastic process' — nothing about development, differentiation or a non-neoplastic tissue.
entries.snippet: Authors conclude that these observations indicate that WWOX is functionally required for cell homeostasis and that its deletion has important consequences contributing to the neoplastic process.

entries.proposition: THE COMPARATOR GENE, AND THE ONLY OTHER CFS GENE PRODUCT THE ISSUE TREATS. FHIT at FRA3B is presented as the mature case of the argument WWOX is the junior case of — a CFS gene product framed as a genome 'caretaker'. Worth keeping because any argument this repository accepts about WWOX-as-caretaker has an older, better-evidenced precedent that can be checked independently: PMID 25283145, unread here.
entries.snippet: Waters and colleagues discussed the accumulative recent evidence suggesting FHIT as a genome ‘caretaker.’

entries.proposition: THE FIELD'S OWN LOAD-BEARING GENOMIC PREMISE, AND IT IS THE SAME TWO PAPERS THE 2015 EDITORIAL RESTS ON. Refs 6 and 7 here are Beroukhim 2010 (PMID 20164920) and Bignell 2010 (PMID 20164919) — which are refs 3 and 4 of PMID 27551470, where they support the claim that WWOX is among the most significantly deleted genes. The same two copy-number papers carry the deletion premise in both wave-5 documents. NEITHER IS HELD IN THIS LEDGER AT ANY DEPTH, and both are queued: they are the actual primary source of a premise this repository has now met twice.
entries.snippet: most of the prevalent recurrent focal deletions target CFS and very large genes

entries.proposition: THE SCALE OF THE OBJECT, USEFUL AS A DENOMINATOR. Approximately 90 common fragile sites in the human genome, of which this issue treats the gene products of exactly two. It bounds how much of the CFS literature can be expected to say anything about any particular gene.
entries.snippet: Up to date, approximately 90 different CFS have been identified in the human genome

entries.proposition: A DATED SELF-ASSESSMENT OF FIELD MATURITY, KEPT WITH ITS DATE ATTACHED. December 2014: the molecular basis and contribution of CFS to cancer development are 'beginning to emerge'. Any inference this repository draws from CFS-framework arguments about WWOX inherits that maturity level as of that date, and the statement is the field's own, not an outside assessment.
entries.snippet: Its only now that the molecular basis and contribution of CFS to cancer development are beginning to emerge.

entries.proposition: THE CHAPTER NUMBERING, QUOTED SO THAT THE ORDERING CHECK BELOW IS ANCHORED. The introduction numbers Gao and Smith's very-large-genes contribution as Chapter 3.
entries.snippet: In Chapter 3, the group of D. Smith focuses on the topic of very large genes and their potential role in cancer development.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE INTRODUCTION'S CHAPTER NUMBERS ARE NOT THE ISSUE'S ORDER, AND THE MISMATCH IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN OCCASIONAL. All nine chapters were resolved to PMIDs with their printed page ranges. Printed order in CMLS 71(23): Le Tallec 4489-94, Ozeri-Galai 4495-506, Franchitto 4507-17, Georgakilas 4519-44, Barlow 4545-59, Savelyeva 4561-75, Waters 4577-87, Aqeilan 4589-99, Gao and Smith 4601-15. The introduction's numbering maps onto that as 2,1,9,3,5,4,7,8,6 — SEVEN OF NINE ARE OUT OF PLACE, and the sharpest case is quoted here: the contribution the introduction calls CHAPTER 3 is the LAST article in the issue, printed after the one it calls Chapter 9. REPORTED AS SMALL, BECAUSE IT IS: it changes no scientific content. It is recorded because it is a trap for exactly this repository — a queue built from these chapter numbers would order the special issue wrongly, and the numbers look authoritative because the editor wrote them.
entries.snippet: In Chapter 2, the group of M. Debatisse
entries.anchor: Body, Chapter 2 summary — quoted as the second anchor of the numbering-versus-pagination check

entries.proposition: THE NINTH CHAPTER'S PREMISE, AND THE ONE PLACE THE ISSUE POINTS AT SOMETHING OTHER THAN CANCER BIOLOGY — 'cancer susceptibility genes' rather than tumour biology. It is still cancer, and it is recorded to show that even the issue's most gene-discovery-oriented chapter does not reach a constitutional or developmental phenotype.
entries.snippet: Being frequent targets of genomic alterations in precancerous lesions, CFS are considered hot spots to identify cancer-related genes.
